annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, and explicit finite-remainder formalization of Theorem 2(a)

assumptions: The total error is the finite sum of the propagated local errors from the paper's telescoping identity.
Each propagated local error has the stated first-order RMS budget and an explicit remainder.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P09 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P09 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p09_t3_multidimensional_rms_error_budget {m n : Nat} (term : Fin m -> Fin n -> Real) (total : Fin n -> Real) (epsilon yRms : Real) (K remainder : Fin m -> Real) ... : p09Rms total <= epsilon * (sum i, K i) * yRms + sum i, remainder i
formal_statement.plain_language: A finite telescoping decomposition of multidimensional FFT error has the sum of its first-order RMS budgets plus the sum of explicit remainders.

informal_proof: Prove a new finite-family Euclidean triangle inequality by induction, divide by the RMS normalization, sum the supplied local bounds, and collect the first-order constants and explicit remainders.
informal_statement: Theorem 2(a)'s multidimensional RMS estimate with every O(epsilon squared) term represented by an explicit finite remainder.

paper_source.local_path: paper_bencmark/reference_papers/P09_Roundoff Error Analysis of the Fast Fourier Transform.pdf

paper_version: published journal version; volume 25, issue 116, October 1971, printed pages 757-768

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The frozen MatrixAlgebra object supplies only the binary Euclidean triangle inequality. A finite-vector-sum theorem exists in NumStability/Analysis/BeneficialRounding.lean but that module is absent from metadata/library_olean.json and is unavailable in condition L; no mounted theorem tracks the explicit finite remainder sum.

source_locations.anchor: Theorem 2(a), its telescoping decomposition, and equation (4.2)

tier_rationale: NumStability.vecNorm2_add_le in NumStability/Analysis/MatrixAlgebra.lean is only a binary adapter. The proof must newly establish the arbitrary finite-family Euclidean bound, transport it through RMS normalization, and collect explicit per-stage remainders. The searched NumStability/Analysis/BeneficialRounding.lean contains a related source theorem, but its object is absent from the frozen library_olean manifest and therefore unavailable.
